as_told.title: Plato's account of Athens fighting Atlantis 9,000 years before

plain: In the writings of the ancient Greek philosopher Plato, a speaker named Critias tells of a great war long ago between ancient Athens and Atlantis, a lost island power. A researcher named James Madden brings it up on the show without naming a source beyond Plato. He calls it a myth, "another good lie", told to Socrates by Critias, and he places it alongside Plato's dialogues the Timaeus and the Republic. Matt LaCroix, a researcher of ancient history, tells it differently. He credits the Greek writer Plutarch as well as Plato, and he presents it as real early history: "proto-Athenians" who actually fought Atlantis. Jesse Michels adds his own detail. He says that in the Timaeus and Critias, the war is set 9,000 years before Plato's time and is told at a festival. If the story were true, it would mean Greece had a forgotten history far older than the one we know.
